It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} recorded in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'', and under the old shrine-ranking system its rank was district shrine. {{nihongo|'''Okada Shrine'''|岡田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shinano Province]].

== Overview ==
The enshrined deity is {{ill|Ukemochi|bcl|Ukemochi|ca|Uke Mochi|da|Ogetsu-no-hime|de|Ukemochi|eo|Uke Moĉi|es|Uke Mochi|eu|Ukemochi|fa|اوکه موچی|hr|Uke Mochi|it|Uke-Mochi|ja|保食神|mni|ꯎꯀꯦꯃꯣꯆꯤ|pl|Ukemochi|pt|Ukemochi|ru|Укэмоти-но ками|sl|Uke-moči|sv|Uke-Mochi|uk|Укемоті|zh|保食神|qid=Q2280323}}. Shrine tradition says it was founded in 654 (Hakuchi 5), and it is considered a shrine that venerates a water spirit deity of the five grains and rich harvest. The approach extends about 600 meters: the first torii stands at the entrance of Okada-juku on the former {{ill|Hokkoku Saigai-dō|ja|北国西街道|qid=Q11401310}}, followed by the second torii, worship hall, and main hall. On both sides of the main hall are 15 massha including Hachiman Shrine. In the early Meiji period, the precinct measured 46 ken east-west and 21 ken north-south. As an inner shrine, Mizuguchi-sha is enshrined upstream on the {{ill|Metoba River|ja|女鳥羽川|qid=Q11446607}}.
